title: Private Access entitlement and the machine tunnel switch
aliases: zpa enabled by default for user tunnel
enable zpa for a group of users

prose.label: Machine tunnels.
prose.text: {{machine-tunnel-for-all}} {{machine-tunnel-disable}} {{machine-token-change}} The machine token is a machine provisioning key: [[zpa.machine-tunnels.provisioning-keys:key-form]].

prose.label: In the API.
prose.text: {{api-field-names}} Whether the group list survives while the all-users switch is on, and becomes effective again when it is turned off, is open {{gap:stale-group-list}}. What the machine tunnel switch does without a Private Access subscription is open {{gap:machine-tunnel-without-zpa}}.
Whether the machine tunnel can be limited to some devices is open {{gap:machine-tunnel-subset}}.

checks.do: Whether ZPA Enabled by Default for User Tunnel is on; if so every user is entitled.
Otherwise whether one of the user's groups is selected, and, where device groups are used, whether the device is in a selected device group as well.
For a pre-login tunnel, whether Enable Machine Tunnel for All is on and the user's app profile carries a machine token.

default-for-all.statement: With ZPA Enabled by Default for User Tunnel on, Private Access is available to all users and cannot be assigned to a group.

quotes: ensure that ZPA Enabled by Default for User Tunnel is disabled. If this setting is enabled, Private Access is available for all users and you cannot assign Private Access to a group.

configurations.statement: With the default off, no user has Private Access unless groups are selected, and then only the selected groups do; by default no user groups are selected.

quotes: | Private Access Enabled by Default | Groups Specified | Behavior |
| Disabled | No | Private Access service is not enabled for any users |
| Disabled | Yes | Private Access service is enabled only for the specified group of users |
By default, no user groups are selected, which indicates that no groups have access to Private Access.

default-by-tenant-age.statement: Private Access instances created before July 2017 have it enabled for all users by default; instances created after July 2017 have it disabled.

quotes: For Private Access instances created before July 2017, Private Access is enabled for all users by default.
For Private Access instances created after July 2017, Private Access is disabled by default.

min-version.statement: Group-level Private Access entitlement needs Client Connector 1.2.4 or later; earlier versions always have Private Access enabled regardless of the setting.

quotes: To enable Private Access for only a select group of users, you must deploy Zscaler Client Connector 1.2.4 or later. However, earlier versions of Zscaler Client Connector always have Private Access enabled, regardless of the Zscaler Service Entitlement setting.

device-and-user-group.statement: When device groups are used, the user must belong to both the device group and the user group, or Private Access disconnects.

quotes: When using device groups, the user must belong to both the device group and user group to avoid disconnecting ZPA services.
the user must belong to both the device group and user group to avoid disconnecting Private Access services.

machine-tunnel-for-all.statement: With Enable Machine Tunnel For All on, all users whose app profile has a machine token can connect to Private Access without being logged in, on Windows or macOS.

quotes: If Enable Machine Tunnel For All is enabled, all users with a Machine Token configured in the app profile can establish a connection to Private Access without being logged in.
You can also configure a machine tunnel to establish a connection to Private Access before users log in to Zscaler Client Connector on a Windows or macOS device.

machine-tunnel-disable.statement: Turning it off does not drop existing machine tunnels: they stay connected until the user's app profile policy is updated and the user logs out.

quotes: any existing machine tunnels remain connected until a user
app profile policy is updated and the user logs out.

machine-token-change.statement: Changing the machine token, or applying a different app profile, does not override existing machine tunnels; the token must be removed from the app profile and the tunnel removed in Enrolled Devices, or the app reinstalled.

evidence.after: The Add Windows Policy window appears.
quotes: Changing the existing machine token, or applying a different app profile to users or groups, won't override the configuration of existing machine tunnels.
You must remove the machine token from the app profile and then remove the machine tunnel in Enrolled Devices in the Zscaler Admin Console or users must reinstall Zscaler Client Connector.

api-field-names.statement: In the API these settings read as `zpaEnableForAll` (the user-tunnel default), `groupList` and `deviceGroupList` (the selections), `computeDeviceGroupsForZPA` (device groups enabled) and `machineTunEnabledForAll`.
api-field-names.conditions: The mapping of API fields to console settings is by name and position; no source states it.

stale-group-list.title: Whether selected groups persist while ZPA is enabled for all users
stale-group-list.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Setting zpa_enable_for_all = true disables the effect of group_list ... If the flag is later toggled back to false, the stale group_list becomes authoritative again and may entitle users who should not have access"; likewise "computeDeviceGroupsForZPA — if false, device_group_list is ignored even if populated" (and the same for ZDX's computeDeviceGroupsForZDX, called a common misconfiguration). The help says groups cannot be assigned while the default is on; it does not say whether an earlier selection is kept, or what a populated list does while its switch is off.
stale-group-list.blocks: auditing who gains Private Access when the all-users default is turned off

machine-tunnel-without-zpa.title: What the machine tunnel switch does without a Private Access subscription
machine-tunnel-without-zpa.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "machine_tun_enabled_for_all is meaningless without a ZPA subscription. If ZPA is not licensed, toggling this flag has no effect."

machine-tunnel-subset.title: Whether the machine tunnel can be enabled for some devices only
machine-tunnel-subset.detail: Unverified legacy statement (references/shared/cross-product-integrations.md): "Machine Tunnel is separately gated (machineTunEnabledForAll) — an all-or-nothing tenant-wide toggle. A tenant that wants Machine Tunnel for a subset of devices doesn't have a group-level knob at the SDK layer we've seen." The help describes only the Enable Machine Tunnel For All switch (claim machine-tunnel-for-all), which applies to users whose app profile carries a machine token; whether the app profile's machine token is itself the per-group control is not stated.
machine-tunnel-subset.blocks: advising how to roll the machine tunnel out to a subset of devices
